questions.title: Which club will Mohamed Salah join first after leaving Liverpool at the end of the 2025–26 season?
questions.background: Mohamed Salah has announced that he will leave Liverpool at the end of the season.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement from Salah or his new club, or reliable news reporting confirming a completed signing. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the first club with which Salah signs a senior playing contract following his departure from Liverpool at the end of the 2025–26 season. Transfer speculation, negotiations, and trial appearances do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the club.
questions.current_reasoning: July 28-30 checks (FootballTransfers July 29; talkSPORT, SI.com, Liverpool.com, TransferMarketWeb July 28; no signing reported on July 29-30) confirm Salah remains unsigned and underline the depth of the Besiktas impasse. Sporting director Onder Ozen publicly declared the Salah file 'temporarily closed and put on the shelf' after President Serdal Adali walked away from the table over Ramy Abbas's image-rights and agent-commission demands, insisting Besiktas 'will not make another offer' while Salah's camp stated they are in talks with another club. With two additional days passing without Salah accepting Besiktas's take-it-or-leave-it offer—and Besiktas unable to match MLS/Saudi money or offer Champions League football—trimming Besiktas 0.28 -> 0.22 (retaining narrow plurality only because three direct meetings with coach Vincenzo Italiano went smoothly and Besiktas left the door open if Salah's camp accepts existing terms). Raising Sporting Kansas City 0.14 -> 0.20 as the sole rival club widely confirmed across talkSPORT, SI.com, and Liverpool.com to hold an active, lucrative two-year offer and open DP slot. Holding Saudi Pro League contenders Al-Ahli (0.14), Al-Hilal (0.12), and Al-Ittihad (0.10) steady with 22% residual for San Diego FC, Al-Qadsiah, Neom SC, or another club.

questions.title: What sentence will Egyptian television presenter Sarah Khalifa receive at trial in her drug-trafficking case?
questions.background: Sarah Khalifa was arrested in Egypt in April 2025 as part of a drug investigation.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The trial court’s announced judgment in the drug-trafficking prosecution stemming from Khalifa’s April 2025 arrest, as confirmed by official court information or reliable reporting from Al-Ahram. Resolution Timing : Resolve when the trial court announces its verdict and sentence. Later appellate decisions and judgments in unrelated cases do not count. Accepted Answer Format : Provide a short legal term identifying the principal penalty imposed, or the court’s disposition if no penalty is imposed. If multiple penalties are imposed, report the most severe.
questions.current_reasoning: Major procedural and legal update from July 8-9 Arabic court reporting (Al-Ahram, Masrawy, Al-Ain, Newsroom): on July 9, the New Cairo Criminal Court adjourned the trial of Sarah Khalifa and 27 co-defendants directly to August 4, 2026 WITHOUT referring the case papers to the Grand Mufti. Under Article 381(2) of Egypt's Code of Criminal Procedure, a criminal court cannot pronounce a death sentence without first referring the file to the Grand Mufti and adjourning weeks later for final sentencing—meaning a death sentence cannot legally be handed down on August 4. Substantively, two further disclosures weaken capital sentencing: (1) Masrawy's indictment summary confirms Khalifa is Defendant #4 (financier/coordinator, plus personal drug-use and unlicensed firearms charges), behind fugitive ringleaders #1 and #2; and (2) defense counsel invoked a Supreme Constitutional Court ruling invalidating scheduling decrees by the Head of the Egyptian Drug Authority. However, the 3-member forensic committee and forensic expert testified on July 8-9 that 2018-2019 Minister of Health decrees explicitly schedule narcotics 'analogues' and confirmed the lab analysis was technically sound, while the court firmly rejected defense procedural challenges. Accordingly, cutting Death penalty sharply 0.28 -> 0.06 (retaining 6% only if the court issues a Mufti referral on Aug 4 for a later verdict), lifting Life imprisonment 0.46 -> 0.56 as the primary statutory penalty under Narcotics Law Art. 33, raising Aggravated imprisonment 0.13 -> 0.19 (Art. 17 clemency or lesser trafficking/firearms counts), Acquittal 0.07 -> 0.11 (Constitutional Court scheduling defense), and Imprisonment 0.04 -> 0.06 (conviction only on drug use/minor counts), with 2% residual.

questions.title: Who will win the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate in Kansas in 2026?
questions.background: Kansas will hold a U.S. Senate election in November 2026, with party nominees selected in the August primary.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Results reported by Kansas election authorities or definitive election reporting from a major news organization. Resolution : Resolve to the winner of Kansas's Democratic U.S. Senate primary scheduled for August 4, 2026, once the outcome is unambiguously reported. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major establishment boost on 2026-07-23 (Kansas City Star): former two-term Kansas Gov. and HHS Secretary Kathleen Sebelius officially endorsed Adam Hamilton 12 days before the Aug 4 plurality primary. The KC Star also confirmed Hamilton's July 13-16 internal poll (n=600) was fielded by reputable Democratic pollster GBAO, giving Hamilton a commanding 30%-13%-10%-5%-2% lead over Christy Davis, Noah Taylor, Patrick Schmidt, and Erik Murray (36% undecided), building on an earlier independent mid-June poll (n>1,000) where Hamilton already led 18%-10%-7%-3%. With mail voting underway, a $3.66M fundraising war chest (>20x rivals), fractured opposition across 11 candidates, and Sebelius's endorsement neutralizing establishment hesitation despite Schmidt's renewed attacks over a 20-year-old church camp allegation (which Hamilton denies), bump Hamilton 0.85 -> 0.89 while trimming Davis (0.06), Taylor (0.025), Schmidt (0.015), and Murray (0.005).

questions.title: Who will win Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate?
questions.background: Michigan will elect a U.S. senator in November 2026. The Democratic primary will determine the party’s nominee for that election.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Results from Michigan election authorities or unambiguous reporting by major news organizations identifying the winner of Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate. Resolution Date : Resolve when the winner of the primary, scheduled for August 4, 2026, is publicly established. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate’s name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major gold-standard polling update on July 30: a new Emerson College Polling/WLNS/WOODTV survey (fielded July 26-27, N=700 likely Democratic primary voters, MOE +/-3.7%) puts Abdul El-Sayed ahead of Rep. Haley Stevens by 15 points, 54%-39% (only 6% undecided), and 57%-41% (+16) with leaners. El-Sayed leads among Democrats (50%-41%), crushes among independents in Michigan's open primary (60%-33%), and dominates voters under 50 (67%-25%), while Gov. Gretchen Whitmer's approval among Democratic primary voters dropped 17 points since April to 62%. Coming one day after Tavern Research's N=914 poll (El-Sayed 46%-36%, +10) and confirming Data for Progress (+13) and Tulchin (+16), four consecutive public polls now show El-Sayed ahead by double digits five days before the August 4 primary. Lifting Abdul El-Sayed 0.74 -> 0.83 and cutting Haley Stevens 0.26 -> 0.17—retaining a meaningful 17% upset path because Emerson still shows voters over 60 breaking for Stevens 53%-39%, leaving turnout composition risk (older mail/absentee electorate), massive pro-Stevens outside spending (~$30M-$50M), and the mid-July Glengariff outlier.

local_articles.title: El-Sayed leading Stevens in Michigan Democratic primary for Senate, poll finds
local_articles.snippet: A new Emerson College poll shows Dr. Abdul El-Sayed leading Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic primary for a U.S. Senate seat. CBS News' Fin Gomez has more on that race and some of the other 2026 midterm battles.

questions.title: Which team will win the second Test of Pakistan's 2026 tour of the West Indies?
questions.background: Pakistan and the West Indies are scheduled to contest a two-match Test cricket series in the Caribbean.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official match result published by the ICC or either national cricket board, corroborated by reputable contemporary match reporting. Resolution : Resolve upon completion of the second Test of Pakistan's 2026 tour of the West Indies, using the final result rather than any intermediate match position. Accepted Answer Format : Provide the winning national team's name. If neither team wins, provide the official result classification.
questions.current_reasoning: Major flip following the 1st Test result and confirmed touring squads (Khaleej Times, Reuters, Cricket West Indies, CricketWinner, July 23-28): West Indies crushed Pakistan by 90 runs on Day 4 at Tarouba on Tuesday July 28, bowling Pakistan out for 120 (after collapsing to 71/9) on the back of Jayden Seales (5/20), Player of the Match Justin Greaves (7/39, historic 5 consecutive wicket-maidens), Shamar Joseph, and Kemar Roach. West Indies now have 2 wins in their last 3 Tests (after beating Sri Lanka 1-0 earlier in July) despite missing Alzarri Joseph and John Campbell. Conversely, Pakistan's actual touring squad is far weaker than our June 24 assumptions — selectors omitted Shaheen Shah Afridi, Naseem Shah, Noman Ali, Hasan Ali, and Saud Shakeel — and first-innings centurion Shan Masood (109) suffered a fractured finger, putting him in serious doubt for Sunday's 2nd Test at Queen's Park Oval (Aug 2-6). Pakistan enter on 4 straight Test defeats, 8 consecutive away Test losses, and 13 losses in 17 Tests, though Mohammad Abbas (5/22 in WI's 2nd innings) and Babar Azam (58*) showed WI's batting remains vulnerable. Given Port of Spain's wet August rainy season and flatter QPO track (recent draws vs India 2016/2023 and South Africa 2024), Draw trims only slightly (0.22 -> 0.20, moderated by both teams' fragile batting in a 4-day 1st Test), while West Indies jump sharply from underdog to clear favorite (0.35 -> 0.51) and Pakistan drop from 0.43 -> 0.29.

questions.title: Who will win the 2026 Republican primary for Tennessee’s 5th Congressional District?
questions.background: Andy Ogles has represented Tennessee’s 5th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives since 2023.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Tennessee election results, with a definitive Associated Press race call accepted before certification. Resolution Event : The determination of the winner of the Republican primary for Tennessee’s 5th Congressional District scheduled for August 6, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major tightening documented across July 20-30 reporting (Axios July 30, Roll Call July 30, Tennessee Lookout July 29, WPLN July 20): clean-energy super PAC Invest in Tomorrow Coalition announced an extra $700,000 final-week blitz on July 30—bringing its pro-Hatcher spend to $2.0M (swamping Freedom Caucus Fund's $500K-$666K)—alongside a July 26-28 Tusk Strategies poll (N=400 likely GOP primary voters, MOE +/-5%) showing Ogles leading Charlie Hatcher by just 4 points, 37%-33% (with ~30% undecided), echoing Hatcher's mid-July internal tie. Hatcher has also outraised Ogles ($720K vs $610K; $105K vs $58K cash on hand as of July 17, with Ogles carrying $70K debt), picked up endorsements from former TN Gov. Bill Haslam and former Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue, and benefits from spring mid-cycle redistricting that shifted TN-5 into drastically new rural/agricultural West-Middle TN territory unfamiliar to Ogles. Kalshi already slid from 90% Ogles in late May to 66% Ogles / 40% Hatcher (~62% normalized) by July 28 before today's Axios scoop. However, Donald Trump held a tele-rally for Ogles on July 28 in a Trump +23 district, PAC-funded polls typically carry pro-challenger lean, early voting has been running since mid-July, and Ogles previously survived a Haslam-backed, better-funded primary challenge by 13 points in 2024. Trimming Andy Ogles sharply 0.78 -> 0.62 and raising Charlie Hatcher 0.22 -> 0.38.

questions.title: Which major US employment sector will shed the most jobs in July 2026?
questions.background: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reports monthly changes in nonfarm payroll employment by sector.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the broad employment sector with the largest net decline in payroll jobs in July 2026, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' initial employment report for that month, released in August 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-07 Accepted Answer Format : Compare sectors by the number of jobs lost, not percentage changes, and count subsectors within their parent sectors. Answer with the sector's name.
questions.current_reasoning: First major update since July 2 incorporating mid-to-late July 2026 US labor and macro data: (1) S&P Global US Flash PMI (July 24, CFO Dive/Trading Economics) jumped to an 8-month high of 53.6 from 51.9, driven by services resuming hiring for the first time in 3 months, while manufacturing slowed to its weakest production growth since March as the resumed US-Iran war (July 7) pushed supplier delays to a ~4-year high and input inflation to a 14-month high; (2) weekly initial jobless claims for the July 12-18 BLS survey week plunged 22k to 187,000 (July 23 Reuters/Straits Times), signaling healthy aggregate private demand; (3) Deloitte Insights (July 19) and FactCheck.org (July 28) confirm federal payrolls fell 324,000 since Jan 2025 (-36k in H1 2026), manufacturing continued declining despite tariffs, gasoline topped $4/gal post-July 7, real spending on food services/accommodation fell two straight quarters ahead of June's -54.6k plunge, while Professional and business services (+23k/mo avg in H1 2026) and wholesale/retail trade actually expanded. With broad private services rebounding, shrinking/shocked and seasonally volatile sectors rise to the top: holding Leisure and hospitality #1 at 0.18 (slightly down from 0.20 on mean-reversion/services PMI rebound, offset by weak dining demand, World Cup winding down from 16 to 4 venues in the survey week, and $4+ gas); lifting Government 0.13 -> 0.17 (persistent federal cuts + huge July state/local education seasonal swings); bringing Manufacturing into the top 5 at 0.15 (replacing Professional and business services, which drops to ~0.09 in residual given H1 +23k/mo trend) on Iran-war supply shocks, ongoing tariff-era contraction, and July auto retooling variance; trimming Financial activities 0.16 -> 0.15 (ongoing YoY contraction and fintech cuts like PayPal/Block/today's Visa 2,600 layoff announcement, though Visa cuts hit later months) and Trade, transportation, and utilities 0.16 -> 0.14 (29M base + $4+ gas tempered by positive 2026 trade trend). 21% residual covers PBS (~9%), Information (~5%), Construction (~4%), Other services (~2%), and others (~1%).
